$comment: The source of sf-alert's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/alert (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

close.x-summary: Dismisses the alert with reason api: sends the cancelable request close first; a page that prevents it keeps the alert

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

accessibility.$comment: The root is a live region (§4.8, §7.4.1): role status (polite) for neutral, info and success, role alert (assertive) for warning and error. Its name is the heading, else the host's aria-label. Tab reaches its action and close buttons.

x-summary: Persistent inline notice with semantic roles, optional actions and dismiss behavior.
x-renamed: settings.title → heading: "title" is a property of HTMLElement.prototype (§3.1, §16 item 26), alias dated
events.action: 1 carried field(s) held the element, not data (§8)
events.sf-alert-action → action (the DOM name without sf-<tag>-)
events.close: 1 carried field(s) held the element, not data (§8)
events.sf-alert-close → close (the DOM name without sf-<tag>-)
settings.type → status, settings.variant → appearance: the axes' old names, dated setting aliases
actions.dismiss → close: one action for one act, a dated action alias

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-alert for persistent inline guidance, warning, error or success feedback inside the page flow.
do_not: Do not use Alert for transient overlay feedback; use Toast
Do not choose a semantic type only for its color
Do not add role=alert to a static message that is already present on page load
Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-alert status="info" title="Update available" supporting-text="Save your changes before refreshing."></sf-alert>

x-decisions: own-verb-words: action is a verb of the alert alone (the person pressed one of its two action buttons; detail.action names which); its word is lang events.action.label. It is a report, not a request the alert waits on, so it is not cancelable.
version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0: title, type, variant and dismiss are dated aliases, close becomes a cancelable request with a reason; a minor while the aliases hold (§4.10).

a11y-role: one live region on the root (§4.8, §7.4.1): status (polite) for neutral, info and success, alert (assertive) for warning and error, written with when on status. The name is the heading, else the host's aria-label (§3.1).

events: close is the request the alert sends before it leaves (cancelable, reason close from its own button or api from close()); a page that prevents it keeps the alert and close() answers refused. The detail carries data only (§8): the element alert leaves it.

x-target text, tone and press (stand 24's record panel note): not added. text and tone would be second names of supporting-text and status, which §4 does not give one setting; a rule binds settings.supporting-text and writes status. press is the alert's action event (action), not a press of the alert.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json plus the statuses and both actions; probe.json drives the close and action buttons, the refused close and the aliases.
skeleton: none; the alert has no port and no late data: its static markup is its first paint (§5.4).
css-variables: the eight public variables the alert sheet already reads (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json).
